environment: Node.js with the actual QR service module, fake localStorage and a mocked Fetch implementation; no network, browser, account or credential.
scenario: Start the real QR exchange with a deliberately held response; complete a real AuthManager sign-out; establish a later authenticated session with different synthetic tokens; release the old exchange response.
assertion: stale QR exchange must not overwrite a later session
result: FAIL (expected red): the delayed service response wrote the old access/refresh tokens and authenticated state over the later synthetic session.
limitations: Service seam with a simulated later session; not a browser journey and not a live exploit.
The screen's post-await stale-session check runs after the service has already published tokens, so the screen check cannot undo this write.
No production source change is recorded in this artifact.
follow_up: CH2 (#118) must port this invariant to a committed lifecycle regression, prove the failure first, and then add attempt/session ownership at the service publication boundary.
